This game got lit the hell up back when it released, but after awhile I think it deserves a bit or grace. For the original trilogy, yes this was a downgrade in effort and quality with some nice touches that could've shone more if the rest was better. I would still recommend it if you wanted more Mass Effect and didn't want to replay the trilogy, but don't expect anything crazy. It at least didn't butcher the series like Veilguard, but it was just very weak in comparison. But 4 may, so this might be the best you get after the first 3. Its solid, plays smooth and all that, ok rpg, but the vision isnt what was before. One thing I will say right away, the ending. Better than the whole rest of the game. Its like they burned out all the inspiration there and couldn't spread it to the rest of the game. The ending is the biggest reason I would say to push through if youre not as pleased. It was pretty good.

I'll be real then give the grace as it isn't a BAD game on its own, just disappointing: 
Graphics and environments were nice, besides the faces which seemed to be worse than ME1, I actually liked the whole idea of the AI-Human learning bond, but the overall plot was very meh, side quests felt empty or meaningless for the most part and didn't feel like it really changed anything, added to other plots, or helped fill the world. Companions were all very boring to me, like mostly everything with Andromeda, if it wasn't Mass Effect, it would've just been a mid open world RPG, but it was Mass Effect. You go from nearly every squad mate you had through the trilogy being good enough for their own expansion, even their own game, to this. They had potential, but they were like all the character ideas that were scrapped or something in the past. It was all very lukewarm. 

The areas suffered from a lazy habit at this time, large, empty, reused assets. The 'we gotta try to be Witcher 3' but lazy at it. Different planets in different systems had the SAME fauna with MAYBE a different color scheme. That's some Final Fantasy 1/Zelda enemy diversity there, without NES hardware constraints. Also, I cant remember but I am pretty sure you get blocked from a lot right away, I feel like I always wanted to explore more but felt like so many 'wait till later' blocks were there. Those can be needed but only if its placed so you don't notice your hard locked out. I don't remember this in the trilogy and I know there were places you couldn't go right away. The main villain enemies are predictable, basic and boring. Big bad aliens that are butthead meanies. Deeeeeep. Theres a bit more to it, some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ moments in any other entry, maybe even the some of the biggest, but it gets so hard to care against everything else.

Also, the Protheans? Old complex tech left by those who came before? Nah man this is a NEW GALAXY. AWAY from all that. OH WAIT, no we're just putting a new skin on it and doing exactly that again.

Special side: THE SIBLING IDEA. Such a missed opportunity that they made sound like they knew what would have been better but didn't do it when they talked about it. Your sibling is 'in the world' well....sure, wouldve been really cool idea to have another you running around in the background, even narrative only, getting other stuff done. But no, well.....technically I guess. It honestly seemed like a huge idea of cut content that they taped over.

What WAS cool: 
I really did like the whole theory to solve AI with a shared experience with organics. It was a cool idea and had potential, even relevance today! Evergreen! Also I liked and disliked being able to be every class and switch. They KIND OF made it believable with biotics if you didn't think too hard about it, but no it wouldn't work that way by their own lore, but it was fun to be able to do anything and multiclass on one character. The combat was fun too, I liked the powers and abilities, felt satisfying, if there were enemies I cared more about fighting. The movement was maybe the only thing that was better than the trilogy, you felt very free to move around and maneuver rapidly. Weapons I would have to look into again but there was a large selection, but I am not big on customizing them and worrying about making them good through piecemeal edits and I think it had a lot of that. So could be good or bad depending on taste. Mako was back, ish, and had some upgrades, it was ok and had some interesting ideas for like 4WD and certain drill and scan stuff.

The space flying to different areas and searching was very dynamic and fun to watch. I went awhile before doing the speed skipping. Looking at stuff you scanned and searching and moving systems was very cool and I looked forward to it each time. WAY better than hearing the neutron bomb of the relay going off in 1. 

You did progress the areas and built them up in your space base and on each planet. That was nice. There was a feeling of developing and solving things in the area to set up a good colony. The different planets did look very distinct, and very appealing. There were different constraints you ran into, some lore searching, they could've really went hard on this because it felt like I wanted more of it or more good info to find about stuff.

The new race you met started very tense and interesting. It felt real. They could've went more into the developing a complex relationship there. But I did like how they did it. I wasn't a big fan of the species personally, but I liked the first contact. The story involving them with no spoilers gets interesting and there are some good twists, but same shadow cast over the rest of the good ideas, the overall lack of care the rest of the game gives really made it hard to be wowed. 

The only side quests I really wish they went more on and felt like FINALLY some good stuff, got cut when the game bombed. There was potential conspiracy and some investigative work behind the scenes, but never was expanded on and resolved. Also some of the other races and their ships were going to get expanded on it seems in DLC but that was cut or cancelled.

The male voice actor was great and I really enjoyed the character. Like Nolan North but wasn't him. Didn't play as the girl so can't say.

Some of the squad had some heart and were interesting but it never went deep enough to really get attached to them. This could potentially be subjective, you may find something you like in some or all of them. They weren't bad, like the theme here, without the ME label and expectation, might have been alright. I only really remember liking two and just wishing I could like others more. Still, they had moments, they did still have their own arcs and motivations. Your crew as well. The trilogy I could see wanting to do different romances because each had potential to be a great partner and have a meaningful arc that way, but not here for me.

There are some references to Shep if you want to find them. Nice touches, makes you miss it though in comparison lol.

THE ENDING. Omg I still remember the finale is better than the whole game put together. Like wtf. I still don't get the contrast. But like I said above, this part was Mass Effect. This felt like something. Its like you woke up from a coma and the rest of the game wasn't real. Such a strange way game series age over time with quality.

Overall, it had the potential and most of the base ideas seemed great. But they were watered down over a huge area with not much going on besides some pockets, and it failed to grasp the enormity of Shepard's story. To be fair that would have been incredibly hard, but they knew, that's why this is in another galaxy. The ideas were there, but not expanded on, and weak ones dragged them down.

If you really love the series, and want to get all of it and can push through lesser stuff, it isn't a bad game at all. Just you KNOW how much better it could have been. I pray for 4, but its hard not to be cynical about old series by now.

I love this game just a little bit more than I find it boring.

I'm definitely not in the camp of people who think this is a terrible game with nothing good about it. Unfortunately, though, I can't say I have much love for it either.

If this game had been a standalone project, I think it would've gotten a lot more love. Unfortunately, it was destined to forever live in the shadow of the original trilogy. And it's not even really unfair, that's the problem. The original trilogy is simply better at pretty much everything that actually matters.

The main story is short, maybe ten to twelve hours, and honestly, it's kind of dull because the game never really manages to challenge you. There are no particularly interesting moral dilemmas or philosophical questions. Hell, even the epic stuff only really shows up towards the very end, when you'd expect the game to have been building towards it from the beginning.

Compared to the Reapers, the Archon is an absolute nothingburger. He can't even come close to creating the same sense of panic or genuine fear that the Reapers did. There's no real intrigue, either. You never get that feeling that maybe you're seriously underestimating your enemy and are about to get punished for it.

I mean, Ryder really is just "I came, I saw, I conquered." Shepard was allowed to make morally questionable decisions, and sometimes even be an absolute bloodthirsty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Shepard could lose, make mistakes, ♥♥♥♥ things up, and generally feel like a much more human character. Ryder, meanwhile, is basically the perfect hero straight off an Alliance recruitment poster.

The direction and cinematography aren't doing the game any favors, either. It often feels like the people making it weren't quite sure what they were doing or what they were supposed to be trying to achieve. Half the scenes feel empty or underdeveloped. There aren't enough interesting camera movements, not enough variety in the shots, and the musical accompaniment feels pretty sparse. It's like the game keeps promising that it's about to show you something important, only to turn away halfway there.

The open world was probably my biggest problem with the game. Visually, it's beautiful and there's plenty to explore, and it seems like it wants to return to the roots of Mass Effect 1. In reality, though, it inherits basically ALL of Dragon Age: Inquisition's worst problems. Fetch quests, pointless resource gathering, and an overall feeling that you're grinding through an MMO.

The companions are also all over the place, ranging from genuinely good and interesting to completely useless and boring. Though, obviously, that's more subjective. What I really wish the game had was more content with them and more opportunities to actually get to know them as people. Even with the romances, the relationships can still feel strangely underdeveloped and blurry around the edges.

So, yeah, this game ABSOLUTELY deserves criticism, but I don't think the way it was completely torn apart was entirely fair. It's not a fundamentally terrible game. It just needed a more competent team and more experienced writers.

However, now that I've pushed forward, it's pretty fun and intriguing. It's not normal Mass Effect, but I'm not mad about it. Ryder will never be Shepard, and that's okay. Not everyone has to be the same.

9/10 - An Amazing Sci Fi Adventure!

I loved every bit of this game. Playing Mass Effect Andromeda was just as enjoyable as watching my favourite sci-fi movies and TV series. The whole experience made me feel like I was part of an epic sci-fi adventure rather than just playing a game. 

If you love sci-fi as much as I do, this game is fantastic experience, I had a great time playing it, and it really captured the feeling of being immersed in sci-fi universe. 

9/10 - An Experience I genuinely loved!
